item.text: South Australia’s Independent Commissioner Against Corruption examined written responses to the Public Integrity Survey 2018 about agency culture and practices.
item.support:
This report examines what public officers had to say, in their own words, about the 
culture and practices of the agencies within which they are employed.

item.text: The Commissioner cautioned that the survey recorded participants’ perceptions and did not establish whether their accounts were true.
item.support: Of course a survey does not prove the truth of the comments made

item.text: The Commissioner reported recurring concerns about fear of reprisals, the usefulness of reporting and the effect of poor workplace conduct.
item.support:
Some participants cast doubt over the utility of 
reporting.

item.text: The Commissioner urged agencies to consult staff, protect reporting and regularly review integrity controls and compliance with policies.
item.support:
Agencies should ensure they regularly revisit their integrity risks to 
monitor their controls to ensure these controls remain fit for purpose.

item.quote:
Agencies have an obligation to create an 
environment where staff are both free to report without reprisal and can be confident 
their reports will be handled appropriately.
